root_cause.text: The `defer_free()` function in the SLUB allocator attempts to write to a freed object using a pointer with an outdated KASAN tag after `kasan_slab_free()` has already poisoned the memory and changed its tag, triggering a false use-after-free report on ARM64 MTE.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds `head = kasan_reset_tag(head);` in `defer_free()` before calling `llist_add(head + s->offset, &df->objects)`, and the commit message explains that "When defer_free() then tries to write to the freed object... the pointer still has the old tag, causing a tag mismatch and triggering a KASAN use-after-free report".

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the `kfree_nolock()` and `defer_free()` functions. In `kfree_nolock()`, `kasan_slab_free()` is called to poison the memory and retag it. Subsequently, `defer_free()` is called (either directly or via `do_slab_free()`), which attempts to write to the object using `llist_add(head + s->offset, &df->objects)`. Because `head` still carries the outdated KASAN tag, this write triggers a false use-after-free (tag mismatch) on ARM64 MTE. The code does not yet contain any untagging mechanism (such as `kasan_reset_tag()`) for `head` in `defer_free()`.
